question.text: An object moves in the x-y plane starting from the location (4 m, 10 m) at t = 0. Its initial velocity vector is given by u = (4î + 8ĵ) m/s, and it experiences a constant acceleration of a = (2î − 4ĵ) m/s². Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: the instant of time at which the object intersects the x-axis.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: the value of its x-coordinate at that specific moment.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: its velocity vector at that exact time.

conditions: crossing the x-axis corresponds to y = 0

figure.description: A 2D Cartesian coordinate plane showing a particle initially at point P(4 m, 10 m). Vectors drawn at point P indicate an initial velocity component of 4 m/s and an acceleration component of 2 m/s² along the positive x-axis, an initial velocity component of 8 m/s along the positive y-axis, and an acceleration component of 4 m/s² along the negative y-axis.

solution.approach: Write the y-coordinate as a function of time and find when it becomes zero, then use that time in the x-coordinate and velocity equations.

steps.text: Write the y-coordinate using the initial y-position, initial y-velocity, and y-acceleration.
Set y(t) = 0 to find when the particle crosses the x-axis, and solve the quadratic, keeping the positive root.
Write the x-coordinate using the initial x-position, initial x-velocity, and x-acceleration, and substitute t = 5 s.
Find the velocity components at t = 5 s using the given accelerations, then combine them for the speed.

common_mistakes.text: Taking t = −1 s, the other root of the quadratic, as the crossing time, which is not physical.
Writing the x-acceleration term as 2t² instead of ½(2)t² = t² gives x(5) = 4 + 20 + 50 = 74 m.
